name: Joe Lombardo
role: Governor of Nevada (since 2023) and former Clark County sheriff (2015–2023)
summary: Lombardo favors market-oriented economic policy, school choice, stronger criminal enforcement and tighter election and immigration controls. His record also includes collective-bargaining support, mental-health investment and some abortion and transgender-care protections, alongside restrictions and vetoes in those areas.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: His pricing veto defends market signals against discretionary government intervention.

unions-good.rationale: He explicitly supports unionization, while opposing compulsory membership and preferential contracting.

regulate-corporations.rationale: He rejects broad new price-enforcement powers as overreach harmful to business investment.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He demands felony penalties for any fentanyl possession and stronger drug laws.

state-harmful.rationale: Endorses Reagan's view that government "can and must provide opportunity" and says state government exists to serve the people.

limit-guns.rationale: He favors background checks, reviewed red-flag orders and carry permits, while rejecting broader gun-control bills as unconstitutional.

empower-police-military.rationale: He proposes increased public-safety pay and stronger enforcement powers.

decide-locally.rationale: Wants education returned from Washington to the states and vetoed bills that took school library and reproductive-health policy from local officials; also vetoed local housing powers.

rehabilitation.rationale: He calls incarceration a last resort and funds treatment, while demanding tougher repeat-offender and drug penalties.

traditional-family.rationale: He describes families as society’s bedrock in his opening remarks.

abortion-legal.rationale: He preserves Nevada’s legal access and opposes a national ban, while personally favoring an earlier gestational limit.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He commits state resources to immigration arrests, removals and eliminating sanctuary barriers.

open-borders.rationale: His signed agreement supports border enforcement and rejects sanctuary policies.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: He rejects rapid clean-energy transition mandates as unaffordable, despite acknowledging human-caused climate change.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He proposes a public fund for strategic economic development and infrastructure.

direct-votes.rationale: Says abortion and voter ID should be decided by Nevada voters and took voter ID to a ballot measure; he calls the legislature his first choice.

school-vouchers.rationale: He supports voucher-style accounts and expanded scholarships for alternative schooling.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: His immigration agreement prioritizes citizens and ends certain services for undocumented residents.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He supports a sex-based restriction on school sports eligibility, a specific public-role distinction.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: As sheriff he expanded body cameras; his department dismissed an officer exposed by footage and settled the victim’s civil-rights claim without admitting wrongdoing.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Record: record education spending, a new health authority, broadband and housing funds, and public safety, well beyond defence, justice and property.

separated-powers.rationale: Cited separation-of-powers limits as a reason to veto AB 490 on court venue.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: He opposes allowing teachers to strike and favors bargaining instead.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He rejects regulating essential-goods price increases as interference with market conditions.

death-penalty.rationale: He explicitly supports execution for egregious crimes, subject to due process.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He acknowledges that tax changes require legislative action rather than unilateral gubernatorial authority.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He supports applying open-meeting and public-records obligations to the state legislature.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He signed transgender healthcare and prison protections, but later opposed provider shields and transgender participation in female sports.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He explicitly rejects defunding street policing and supports continued incarceration for serious offending.

rent-control.rationale: He explicitly vetoes rent caps, arguing they discourage supply and worsen affordability.

future-generations.rationale: He calls for protecting Lake Tahoe so future generations can enjoy it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: He prefers negotiated collective agreements to government-mandated changes in union benefits.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: He supports Nevada’s right-to-work law and opposes repealing it.

voter-id.rationale: He actively promotes and funds a ballot proposal requiring voter identification.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: His budget proposes suspending fuel tax to reduce motorists’ costs.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He defends directing free-meal funding to demonstrated need rather than universal eligibility.

notes:
Reviewed sheriff-era body-camera accountability and 2022 interview, downloaded complete 2023 address and searched every theme, then checked 2024 interviews, primary 2025 vetoes and immigration agreement, and 2026 campaign reporting. All 490 statements reviewed, including remaining nulls. Early openness to rent control is superseded by explicit later opposition. Abortion protection and personal restriction preferences coexist; transgender healthcare protections and sports restrictions are both retained. Opposition to one price-fixing bill is not blanket endorsement of cartels. Collective bargaining support does not erase restrictions on teacher strikes or union-only contracting. Need-based meals do not establish elimination of welfare. Immigration enforcement is not a complete ban on legal migration or a racial deportation doctrine. Stronger habitual-offender sanctions do not by themselves establish fixed sentences without judicial discretion. Public-option opposition is not conclusive evidence against every model of universal coverage; detailed national healthcare and monetary views remain unknown. Undersheriff Kevin McMahill’s 2015 interview remarks were not assigned to Lombardo. No inferred answers.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 5 answers taken from it, 21 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Second, independent pass. Searched: both State of the State addresses (2023, 2025), the 2023 and 2025 veto messages (about 160 PDFs, read by topic), 150 press releases and executive-order notes, KTNV, KNPR and Nevada Independent interviews and debate coverage. World-affairs and most culture and philosophy statements have no stated position and stay null; no Alex Jones Show guest segment was found (corpus hits are mentions only). Right-to-work and tariffs rest on reports or narrow cases and are null here. Answers resting on vetoes use his own veto reasoning; a veto message is read only for the reason it gives. 2022 candidate positions (abortion, guns, public option) come through news transcripts, flagged as reference sources.
